title: Write-off discharges all four outstanding buckets over the eleven UNPAID instalments (loan 13: 92115.12 principal / 5618.53 interest / 100.00 fee / 57.00 penalty) and the four portions sum to the amount 97890.65, while the fully paid period 1 contributes 0
_note: Parity vector transcribing a SECOND observed loan write-off, on the running Fineract server under tenant gerege (loan 13, externalId OHWOPAID-L01, product 3 OHLGR-Accrual-Loan, ACCRUAL PERIODIC) at business date 2026-09-03. Unlike loan 11, loan 13's schedule has ONE fully paid instalment (period 1, complete true, obligationsMetOnDate 2026-02-01) and eleven unpaid ones. request.write_off.installments transcribes the loan's repayment schedule read back AFTER the single repayment, in out/loan-13-after-repay-detail-raw.json repaymentSchedule.periods[1..12], each period's principalOutstanding / interestOutstanding / feeChargesOutstanding / penaltyChargesOutstanding, raised to integer minor units; period 1 carries obligations_met true and its OBSERVED post-repayment cells 0/0/0/0. expect.write_off_allocation and expect.write_off_total_minor are TRANSCRIPTIONS of the write-off transaction's four portions and its amount in out/loan-13-after-transactions-raw.json content[id 57] (type.code loanTransactionType.writeOff, date 2026-09-03): principalPortion 92115.12, interestPortion 5618.53, feeChargesPortion 100.0, penaltyChargesPortion 57.0, amount 97890.65. The four portions sum EXACTLY to the amount (9211512 + 561853 + 10000 + 5700 = 9789065), and the after-state out/loan-13-after-detail-raw.json sets all four *_outstanding buckets to 0.00 and all four *_writtenOff derived buckets to those same amounts (status loanStatusType.closed.written.off, id 601). THIS VECTOR GRADES ONE PROPERTY: a write-off discharges the outstanding of EVERY unpaid instalment into ALL FOUR buckets, and the four portions sum to the write-off amount. The observed fee (100.00) and penalty (57.00) are NON-ZERO and DIFFERENT, so the same drives as the loan-11 vector are discriminated: writes off only principal; writes off principal + interest; drops the fee bucket; drops the penalty bucket; and swaps fee and penalty. WHAT THIS VECTOR DOES NOT GRADE: the obligationsMet skip itself. The input is the OBSERVED post-repayment state: the fully paid period 1 has all four outstanding cells 0, so a port that skips paid-off instalments and a port that forgets the skip sum the SAME twelve rows and both return 9789065 — the skip is a mathematical no-op on this observed input and NO skip drive is registered. The vector deliberately does NOT pair the pre-repayment outstanding of period 1 (P 788488 + I 100000 in out/loan-13-before-detail-raw.json) with its post-repayment obligations_met flag: that combination is a synthesised input, not an observation, and this vector transcribes what the oracle actually read back. OUT OF SCOPE for this capture seam: the five-leg write-off journal entry L57 (one DEBIT OHLGR-Losses-Written-Off, four credits) and the write-off transaction's own read-back; each is a separate observation and neither is touched here. Nothing was computed by this promotion: every instalment cell and every expected cell is read directly from the committed files.

provenance.note: request.write_off.installments is transcribed from the committed AFTER-REPAYMENT repayment schedule in out/loan-13-after-repay-detail-raw.json (GET /loans/13?associations=all, HTTP 200); expect.write_off_allocation and expect.write_off_total_minor are transcribed from the write-off transaction id 57 in out/loan-13-after-transactions-raw.json (HTTP 200), cross-checked against the after-state out/loan-13-after-detail-raw.json (HTTP 200). The write itself is req/loan-13-writeoff.json (POST /loans/13/transactions?command=writeoff). The captures are single-line JSON documents, so the observation is cited at line 1. capture_case_id names the loan's externalId OHWOPAID-L01, which appears in the referenced after-repay-detail capture. No value was synthesised: the instalment cells and the four portions are read directly from the files.
